headline: GOLDEN HANDSHAKE: Two More Mining Companies Announce Merger as Gold Tops $4,600
snippet: Bloomberg's mining newsletter reports another pair of mining companies have reached deal terms, adding to an accelerating wave of consolidation driven by record gold prices. The announcement comes as the sector records $21.6 billion in M&A across 121 Q1 deals.

headline: RARE EARTHS AMERICAS Raises $63M in Oversubscribed NYSE Debut — $368M Valuation
snippet: Rare Earths Americas completed an oversubscribed IPO on the NYSE American exchange on May 13, raising $63.3 million at its target $368 million valuation to advance four exploration-stage heavy rare earth projects across Brazil and the U.S.

headline: SILVER WHIPSAWS: 6% Tariff-Truce Surge Erased as April CPI Prints Hot at 3.8%
snippet: Silver gave back most of its explosive single-session gain from May 11 — when the U.S.-China 90-day tariff truce briefly sent it above $87 and compressed the gold/silver ratio below 55 — after April CPI came in at 3.8%, above expectations, dragging silver back toward the low $80s.

headline: COPPER SLIPS 1.5% on May 14 But Holds Near All-Time Highs — Up 40% in 12 Months
snippet: Copper eased to $6.53/lb on May 14, pulling back 1.53% in a single session but remaining within striking distance of all-time highs. The metal has gained more than 40% year-over-year on resilient Chinese industrial demand, AI data-center build-out, and supply disruptions tied to sulfuric acid export restrictions.

headline: CHINA SILVER DEMAND: 790+ Tons Imported in Early 2026 — SIL ETF Breaks Key $43 Resistance
snippet: China's silver imports are on pace for a record year in 2026, driven heavily by solar panel manufacturing, with over 790 tonnes absorbed in the first months of the year. Silver miners tracked by the SIL ETF surged 6.56% and broke decisively above the key $38–$43 resistance zone before the CPI-driven pullback.

headline: NdPr OXIDE DROPS 21% IN APRIL to $99.61/kg — Still 88% Above January Open
snippet: Neodymium-praseodymium oxide suffered its sharpest monthly decline since the Q1 rally began, falling 21% in April to $99.61/kg. Despite the correction, NdPr prices remain well above the cost base of major Western producers including MP Materials and Lynas, which holds strategic significance for new project economics.

headline: GOLDMINING Turns Two Rigs at São Jorge — 8,000m Fully Funded Program Kicks Off in Brazil
snippet: GoldMining Inc. (TSX: GOLD) has commenced a fully-funded, two-rig, 8,000-metre drill program at its São Jorge project in the Tapajós gold district of Pará State, Brazil. The program targets extensions of known gold mineralization in one of South America's most prolific gold-producing regions.

headline: ENERGY STORAGE to Drive 55% Lithium Demand Jump in 2026 — But Prices Stay Beaten Down
snippet: Lithium demand from grid-scale energy storage is forecast to surge 55% in 2026, following 71% growth in 2025, as battery deployment accelerates globally. Despite the demand tailwind, persistent oversupply continues to keep spot prices well below their 2022 peak — a disconnect that creates a potential long setup for patient investors.

headline: MINING M&A HITS $21.6B in Q1 2026 Across 121 Deals — Gold Still the Top Target
snippet: Mining sector M&A maintained strong momentum through Q1 2026, recording 121 transactions worth a combined $21.6 billion — up year-on-year. Gold remained the most targeted commodity while supply-chain security and critical minerals access drove deal structures, with strategic partnerships expected to dominate the rest of 2026.

headline: WHY INSTITUTIONAL FORECASTERS Still See Gold at $5,000 — Despite the Pullback
snippet: With gold consolidating around $4,688 after touching $4,739, major institutional forecasters are holding their $5,000 targets, citing structural support from central bank accumulation at record levels, persistent dollar weakness, and a supply side constrained by near-peak global mine output.

headline: BARRICK MINING: Strong Q1 Beats Revenue by $380M — But Valuation Has No Margin of Safety
snippet: Barrick delivered a Q1 beat of $380M in revenue and $0.17 on EPS, yet one analyst argues the stock offers no margin of safety at current prices — questioning whether high gold translates to shareholder returns when peers like Agnico Eagle are reporting $1,483/oz AISC against a $4,861/oz realized price.

headline: STOP CHASING $87 SILVER: The Structural Deficit That Matters More Than the Price Swings
snippet: With silver whipsawing on tariff headlines and CPI prints, one analyst argues retail investors are being distracted by short-term price action. The real story is the sixth consecutive year of structural supply deficit, an ongoing gap that weekly macro noise cannot resolve.
